newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, looking to Washington.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, looking to Washington.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat in early trade Monday, getting off to a slow start after last week's big rally, as traders looked to Congress to provide more details about the budget accord agreed to last Friday.
"Prices are basically flat so far," a trader said. "What's going to happen with the budget accord?" he added, when asked what the week's pressing concerns were.

After last week's volley of data, which gave hope to the rose-colored glasses contingent by showing that the economy was growing faster than expected but without sparking inflation, the reports due this week were not seen as quite as likely to prompt big reactions in fixed-income markets.

Nuveen Municipal Market Comments said that the "vision of the Goldilocks economy" has shifted expectations that the Federal Reserve policy-making arm will raise interest rates at its May 20 meeting to a 50 to 50 likelihood, down from an 80 to 20 proposition.

Municipal bond sales for the week of May 5 were expected to total $4.1 billion in 102 sales, the largest dollar total since $4.5 billion was offered the week of April 7, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

While most of the deals will not start hitting the market in volume until Tuesday, negotiated offerings for the week were expected to total $3.3 billion in 42 sales, with a $486 million San Antonio, Texas, deal through PaineWebber Inc. topping the list.
Another capstone for the week will be a $350 million sale of revenue bonds by the New York State Thruway Authority, traders said.
On the competitive side, 60 sales totaling $749 million are on the schedule. A $173 million Tennessee deal on Wednesday is the largest.
An additional 11 sales totaling $646 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds this week depending on market conditions.
Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.72 percent, NET, down one basis point.
And bids for Port Authority of New York and New Jersey JFK International Air Terminal revenues of December 2022, which pay a 5.75 percent coupon, were unchanged at 5.94 percent, NET.
In debt futures, June municipal bond futures firmed three ticks to 115-1/32, while June Treasury bonds edged up one tick to 109-30/32. This left the MOB spread at 163 ticks.
